content.user_title: Research Game Project Management with PMNote
content.value_statement: Game project managers need reliable context for delivery decisions, career preparation, and AI tool choices. PMNote connects public references with sourced analysis and practical next steps.
actual_capabilities: Find relevant public PMNote articles, guides, terminology, podcasts, and job references through categorized directories.
Search current public work metadata by title, summary, topic, or media type and retrieve linked platform versions.
Retrieve published interview accounts through anonymous list and detail requests while preserving contributor attribution.
Read public work-thought issues and current AI tool descriptions using the bundled Python reader.
Develop schedule reviews, risk lists, and retrospective outlines from public sources and user-provided project facts.
Separate source viewpoints from recommendations and distinguish summaries from full articles or transcripts.
limitations: Live content retrieval needs network access; the bundled reader requires Python 3.9 or later.
The reader does not provide private account access, publishing, administration, or paid course materials.
Work searches cover metadata rather than full program transcripts; podcast summaries do not establish every spoken viewpoint.
Project advice depends on supplied facts; job availability, tool capabilities, and service details require current source verification.

use_cases.title: Review a Game Release Plan
use_cases.description: Compare a proposed milestone plan with relevant public guidance and identify missing dependencies, delivery risks, and follow-up decisions.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Game PM Interviews
use_cases.description: Use attributed public interview accounts and role references to organize practice questions and identify gaps in project examples.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Art Production AI Tools
use_cases.description: Read current tool descriptions and related public sources to compare workflow fit, limitations, and questions for a trial.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Game PM Role
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain game project management using public PMNote sources. Cite the material you read and suggest three beginner learning priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Interview Practice Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Find public PMNote interview material for [company or role]. Attribute contributors and separate reported questions from your recommendations. Build a practice plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Milestone Schedule
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this game milestone plan: [sanitized plan]. Consult relevant public PMNote articles. List risks, dependencies, proposed checks, and unknown facts without inventing dates.

prompt_templates.title: Design an AI Workflow Trial
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate AI options for [game production workflow] under [constraints]. Verify current tool descriptions. Propose a trial with acceptance criteria, risks, and unresolved evidence.

output_examples.input: Where should I start learning about the game PM role?
output: Starting reference: Game PM Complete Guide, https://pmnote.ai/articles/game-pm-complete-guide.md.
Review the source for role responsibilities, then identify which responsibilities match your target position.
Use a real project example to list goals, dependencies, and decisions you would need to coordinate.

output_examples.input: Review a milestone plan that lists tasks but omits owners, staffing, and testing time.
output: Review outline: assign an owner to each deliverable and identify its upstream dependencies.
Capacity remains unknown until staffing and effort estimates are supplied.
Testing time is unspecified, so the release date cannot be assessed reliably.
Next step: request capacity estimates and acceptance criteria before revising the schedule.

best_practices: Provide sanitized project goals, constraints, dependencies, and known dates before requesting a schedule or risk review.
Ask for original source links, contributor attribution, and clear separation between evidence and recommendations.
Use generic public search keywords and verify current job, tool, or service details before making decisions.
anti_patterns: Sending resumes, contact details, or confidential project information as public interview search keywords.
Treating titles, metadata summaries, or podcast shownotes as evidence of unread full content.
Using the skill for unspecified product management questions or expecting private content access and guaranteed career outcomes.

faq.question: Does PM mean product manager in this skill?
faq.answer: No. This skill focuses on game project management. Ambiguous product management requests need clarification.

faq.question: Which assistants are supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Available browsing and command permissions determine which reading methods can run.

faq.question: Does the reader need a login?
faq.answer: No. It reads public sources and uses the anonymous website configuration for published interview entries. It does not read private account tokens.

faq.question: What software is required?
faq.answer: The bundled reader requires Python 3.9 or later and uses standard-library modules. Public pages can also be opened with browsing tools.

faq.question: Can it provide full podcast transcripts or paid lessons?
faq.answer: Not as a general capability. It distinguishes public summaries from full content and does not provide paid course materials.

faq.question: Can it verify that jobs and tool details are current?
faq.answer: It directs the assistant to check current pages and official sources. Local directories alone do not establish availability or current capabilities.
